evidence.why: Validation occurs within the mutating loop; the updater call follows the loop without an empty-chain guard.

facts.rationale: Preserves the existing guards and completion behavior while documenting useful empty-chain and partial-mutation exceptions.
facts.value: Asserts a valid channel and returns CARD_RESULT_NOCARD for a detached card. Traverses until 0xFFFF, validating each block before reading its next link, clearing its entry and incrementing fat[3]. An invalid block returns CARD_RESULT_BROKEN without rolling back entries or free-count increments already changed. An initial 0xFFFF skips traversal but still starts FAT persistence. Successful traversal returns the immediate result of __CARDUpdateFatBlock.

evidence.why: Preparation and callback assignment precede a direct erase-start return.
Defines currentFat re-fetch, write initiation, success-only rotation and guarded terminal cleanup.

facts.rationale: Corrects the unqualified statement that failures complete immediately and preserves the distinct asynchronous lifetime and ownership branches.
facts.value: After asserting the channel, increments fat[2], recomputes checksums, stores the cache range and saves eraseCallback before returning __CARDEraseSector's immediate result. There is no local cleanup or rollback on an initial erase-start failure. If erase completion is delivered successfully, EraseCallback re-fetches currentFat and starts its write. Negative erase completion or immediate write-start failure takes terminal cleanup; WriteCallback handles write completion, switching and synchronizing the alternate RAM FAT only for a nonnegative result. Terminal callback paths release the control block only when apiCallback is absent and clear a non-null eraseCallback before invoking it.

evidence.why: Shows all mutation orderings, direct error returns and callback success/error paths.

facts.rationale: Makes the unit summary accurately distinguish RAM mutation, persistence initiation and asynchronous completion instead of implying transactional error recovery.
facts.value: Allocation and freeing reject detached cards, but corruption detection is interleaved with RAM mutation and does not roll back earlier changes. Allocation reserves the free count before scanning; freeing validates and clears one link at a time. Persistence updates integrity metadata and saves a callback before returning the immediate erase-start result, without local cleanup on that initial failure. Callback-delivered erase errors, immediate write-start errors and write completions use guarded control-block release and clear-before-call completion. Only a nonnegative write completion switches currentFat to the alternate 0x2000-byte RAM image and synchronizes it; negative completion does not reverse prior mutations.
